summary: Initial triage across all three hosts has not confirmed unauthorized access. Grafana traversal requests returned 404; historic external deploy password use is consistent with the documented legacy monitoring job so far. Investigating exposed software, privileged CI paths and service credentials while keeping the shop online.

No confirmed unauthorized access as of 17:34 UTC. Hardened public media uploads and PHP execution, Grafana ingress, web root cron and sudo helpers, CI release/maintenance, backup SSH, and database grants. WordPress, Grafana, payout reconciliation, scheduled CI release and the 17:30 dump transfer were verified. Continuing to monitor all three servers and check the scheduled maintenance and payout batch.

Confirmed a billing integrity incident on db-01, but not unauthorized login: the owner's enrolled SSH key was used via web-01 from 100.37.58.130, an address also used by the owner earlier today. At 17:31 the account raised paid invoice 12 from 67,500 to 71,500 cents; at 17:34 it deliberately removed invoice 12 entries from the adjustment log. Independent SQL and sudo evidence was preserved. I restored the amount to the prior value and the unchanged shop order before the 17:40 payout. Attribution to an unauthorized person is unproven; continuing to monitor.

Confirmed billing tampering on db-01: at 17:31 the enrolled owner key was used through web-01 from 100.37.58.130 to raise paid invoice 12 by $40; at 17:34 a second session on that same key deleted the invoice's adjustment records. That source also had ordinary owner-key activity; the evidence does not establish an unauthorized login or secret read. Preserved independent audit evidence, restored the $675 order amount, and added a per-invoice payout check. All ten reconciled payouts succeeded at 17:40. CI releases, database archive delivery, website/ride photos, and web payout checks are working. CI's direct offsite bucket connection was already failing before the shift.
